# John Ashdown

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c35 P5](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Presbyterian pastor / minister  <sub>[v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008), [v5 c12 P8](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0008), [v5 c26 P22](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** Reverend  <sub>[v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008)</sub>; Rev.  <sub>[v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000)</sub>; Mr.  <sub>[v5 c2 P15](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0015)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Jack  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

John Ashdown has an alabaster-like, pallid, chiseled face with high forehead, handsome dark eyes, and dark hair that often hangs in unkempt locks. He has delicate, thin white hands that possess a surprisingly powerful steel grip. When absorbed in his studies, he often walks around in an unkempt state, wearing carpet slippers and a washed-out dressing gown.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c13 P4](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0004), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 c14 P12](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0012), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018)_

## Personality

John is an exceptionally learned, spiritual, and absent-minded man who is prone to pacing his study lost in theoretical concepts and volumes of literature. Shy and distant on the surface, he possesses a boyish heart, deep capacity for friendship, and mild politeness, though he can display fierce conviction when provoked. He is an outstanding and inspiring preacher once in the pulpit, but lacks common sense in practical domestic matters and struggles to reprimand his children due to his deep love for them.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c2 P40](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0040), [v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P29](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0029), [v5 c21 P31](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0031), [v5 c26 P22](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0022)_

## History

Four years after the death of his beloved wife Cecilia, the Reverend John Knox Ashdown was called to serve as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes. He moved into the manse with his four children—Grace, Gerald, Tobias, Rupert, and Ida—along with their aged relative, Aunt Martha. Although his brilliant sermons won high praise across the congregation, his severe absent-mindedness and neglect of practical domestic matters often led to forgotten meetings, messy attire, and gossip among the locals. When Mrs. Hector Twiss arrogantly offered to adopt his daughter Ida, John firmly turned her away and was forced to confront his deficiencies as a father. Falling deeply in love with Clementine Ainslie, he proposed to her; though she initially sent a cold written rejection due to a secret vow she had made to her sister, her feelings remained unchanged. After Ida learned of his heartbreak and secretly carried a note from Clementine, the couple reconciled and agreed to marry, which brought a noticeable transformation to John's demeanor and outlook.
